security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel code (e.g., in capability-aware copyin/copyout, signal frame setup, or cheriabi bounds narrowing) emits SCBNDSI with an immediate operand that requires a bound value >256 bytes, which the pre-shrink 10-bit encoding supported (up to 3840) but the new 8-bit encoding can only represent as values 1-256. The compiler or assembler targeting the new spec would either reject the instruction or silently encode a truncated/clamped value, producing a capability with bounds tighter than the kernel intended.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: search for SCBNDSI (or .4byte encodings matching the old 10-bit immediate format with funct2=00 and non-zero upper bits in the former uimm[9:8] field) in kernel assembly, including inline assembly in copyin/copyout paths, signal trampoline setup, and capability narrowing macros; also audit cheriabi bounds calculations that derive SCBNDSI immediates from user-supplied buffer lengths where the length could legitimately exceed 256 bytes
security_spec.summary: SCBNDSI immediate shrunk from 10-bit (max bound 3840) to 8-bit (max bound 256); FreeBSD's 'almost all' coverage means kernel code paths using SCBNDSI for bounds >256 bytes (e.g., copyin/copyout of larger buffers, signal frame capability setup) would silently produce overly-tight capabilities, causing unexpected capability faults and kernel denial-of-service
